metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness persists each pending provider retry, but the DSH adapter skips llm/retry records and cannot paint the required retry window red.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: bug
driver_capability: ready

## Scenario signal

The scenario requires one stable session to follow ready -> working -> error -> ready. The session must enter error when the first provider retry is scheduled, stay in error across later attempts, never enter waiting, and return to ready only after a successful turn/end.

## Agent support

DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 implements this behavior explicitly. The installed dsh-base composition mounts dsh-llm-retry. The installed retry package documents a default normal policy with five retries for RATE_LIMIT, SERVER, TIMEOUT, TRANSPORT, and EMPTY_RESPONSE. Its implementation appends a durable llm/retry record before each backoff and a durable llm/retry-started record before the next attempt. The pi-ai adapter maps messages containing a 5xx status to SERVER, so HTTP 529 is eligible.

This is also measured behavior. The committed DeepSeek Harness 2-14 transcript contains five llm/retry records and five llm/retry-started records with increasing delays before the final failed turn/end. The failure there is TRANSPORT rather than HTTP 529, but it proves that the installed agent loop emits the documented durable retry records on the exact TUI profile that this recipe drives.

## Daemon capability

The DSH adapter mishandles the available trace. core/adapters/inbound/agents/dsh/parser.go declares handlers for session, turn, approval, message, tool, and request records only. ParseLine sets Skip=true for every unknown type. Therefore it discards both llm/retry and llm/retry-started.

The committed 2-14 recording gives concrete daemon evidence. Its transcript records retry scheduling from lines 18 through 31. Its events.jsonl enters working at sequence 255, emits transcript activity throughout the retry ladder, and does not enter error until sequence 420, after the terminal error turn/end. Thus the daemon does not paint a pending retry red even though the source contains the required signal.

This is a bug, not an architectural limit. tailer.SessionError already has ErrorPhaseRetrying, Attempt, MaxAttempts, RetryIn, Class, and Message. A successful turn_done already clears a retrying error. The DSH parser must map llm/retry to that existing shape. The spec remains known-failing and asserts the correct arc.

## Driver capability

The recipe uses send, wait_turn, sleep, and exit_clean. The DeepSeek Harness interactive driver declares and implements all four steps. The driver also accepts model, base_url, context_window, permission_mode, and api_key settings and writes them into a temporary OpenAI-compatible provider patch. Therefore the script driver is ready.

The repository does not yet contain an OpenAI Chat Completions mock that fails the first N primary requests and then succeeds. The existing mock-openai-429 succeeds first and fails every later request, which is the opposite lifecycle. This missing mock is a recording prerequisite, not a driver step gap. The recipe names the required mock contract so record can run after that prerequisite is supplied. The mock must ignore DSH's concurrent session-title request when it counts failures, or that side request can consume a retry slot and make the cell prove the wrong behavior.
caveats: Vacuous-pass condition: the cell would pass without proving provider retry if the mock served the main request successfully on its first attempt or if a session-title request consumed the configured failure slots. The transcript spec therefore requires exactly three llm/retry records with failure.code SERVER, and the mock must count only primary turn requests.

Load-bearing prerequisite: add tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-openai-overload. It must serve /v1/chat/completions, fail the first three counted primary requests with HTTP 529, then stream one successful completion with non-zero usage. It must answer but not count the concurrent title-generation request.

The committed measured retry fixture uses TRANSPORT failures, not HTTP 529. The installed pi-ai adapter source maps 5xx error text to SERVER, and the installed retry policy includes SERVER. A live recording must confirm that the new mock produces that exact durable failure code.

The model observation is intentionally not pinned. The driver selects qwen/qwen3.5-9b, but the prospective mock does not yet exist and can control the model label in its response. Record must fill the exact model from the live recording.
The llm/retry record means that another attempt is scheduled. It does not prove recovery. The transcript assertions separately require one completed turn/end and forbid an error turn/end.
The five-second post-turn sleep matches the longest committed sibling delay. It gives irrlichd time to publish the recovered ready state before exit_clean removes the live process.

Load-bearing isolation precondition: the driver must keep its fresh per-run cwd and pre-launch marker, and run-cell.sh must verify that the mock served counted primary requests. Otherwise another DSH transcript or the real provider could satisfy the lifecycle phases.

sources.note: Installed 0.1.5-rc.2 package contract: default normal mode retries RATE_LIMIT, SERVER, TIMEOUT, TRANSPORT, and EMPTY_RESPONSE up to five times, and each scheduled attempt reaches the durable session log before backoff.
The shipped backoff function appends llm/retry before its cancellable delay and llm/retry-started before returning retry to the agent loop.
The shipped pi-ai adapter classifies error text containing 429 or rate-limit as RATE_LIMIT and text containing any 5xx status as SERVER. Both codes are retryable under the default policy.
Measured DSH 0.1.5-rc.2 trace: lines 18-31 contain five durable llm/retry and llm/retry-started pairs with retry numbers 1-5 and increasing delayMs values before the terminal failed boundary.
Concrete daemon result for the measured retry trace: ready->working at sequence 255, no error during the five scheduled retries, then working->error only at sequence 420 after terminal turn_done.
recordHandlers has no llm/retry or llm/retry-started entry. ParseLine marks every unrecognized record Skip=true. parseTurnEnd handles only the eventual completed or terminal boundary.
SessionError already represents retrying failures with attempt, maximum-attempt, retry-delay, class, and message fields; ClearedByTurnBoundary clears ErrorPhaseRetrying on the eventual turn_done.
ErrorPhaseRetrying is the domain shape for holding a session red for the whole retry window rather than flickering per attempt.
Declares and implements send, wait_turn, sleep, and exit_clean. It applies the recipe model, base URL, context window, permission mode, and API key through a temporary provider patch.
The only Chat Completions mock succeeds on request one and fails every later request. It cannot elicit fail-N-then-recover, so a separate stateful mock is required.

preconditions: dsh >=0.1.5-rc.2 is installed and on PATH
the community TUI profile is installed under ~/.dsh/profiles/tui
tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-openai-overload exists and implements the mock contract in this assessment
port 18805 is free on 127.0.0.1 at record time
irrlichd is recording the deepseek-harness adapter
setup: run-cell.sh builds and launches mock-openai-overload on 127.0.0.1:18805 before the driver starts

the mock ignores the DSH title-generation request for failure counting, fails the first three primary POST /v1/chat/completions requests with HTTP 529, and succeeds on the fourth with an ok completion and non-zero usage
the interactive driver creates a fresh cwd and pre-launch marker, applies a temporary OpenAI-compatible provider patch for the mock, and launches dsh --profile tui in tmux
the driver resolves only the post-marker compressed transcript whose session header has the fresh cwd

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: the same DSH session follows ready -> working -> error -> ready and never enters waiting
the durable transcript contains exactly three llm/retry records with failure.code SERVER before one completed turn/end
the session enters error once and stays there across the complete retry window
the completed turn clears the retrying error and leaves the session ready before exit_clean
the mock log proves that the primary turn reached the mock four times and that title traffic did not consume the failure counter
the live observation vector reports non-zero tokens and zero known cost; record fills the exact model from the recording
recipe.scope_note: Uses the muse sibling's five-second post-turn sleep, the longest committed sibling delay. The claudecode sibling has no sleep, but DSH writes compressed frames and the hold keeps recovery observable before exit_clean. The 180-second timeout matches both committed sibling recipes and exceeds the default three-retry backoff window by a wide margin.
